_note: Constants for Diplomacy (scripts/sim/diplomacy.gd). Opinions run -100..100 between two nations; each pair has a baseline (from blocs and treaties, or set in the scenario) that the opinion drifts back to.

treaties._note: Directed treaties run from a to b (a guarantees b, a lets b's armies cross); the rest bind both. relation_bonus is added to the pair's baseline while the treaty stands.

war._note: Declaring a war (Diplomacy.declare_war). A casus belli sets what a declaration costs: target_relations is added to the target's opinion of the aggressor and world_relations to every other nation's; prestige goes to the aggressor. 'none' is always allowed. unprovoked_aggression is not declared on, it is earned: a war with no casus belli gives it, for cb_years, to the aggressor's land neighbours and the guarantors of its victim.

cancel._note: What it costs the cancelling nation to tear up a treaty: partner_relations (the other party's opinion), world_relations (everyone else's), prestige.

join._note: Join decisions (Diplomacy.offer_joins). A declaration offers every ally and guarantor of the nations in the war a choice. Bound obligations are alliance_defence (the original target was attacked), alliance_called (an ally at war calls you; defensive-only alliances are not bound by it), and guarantee (the original target is a guaranteed nation). An entente is optional: an AI nation joins when its opinion of an enemy is at or below entente_join_relation. Declining a bound obligation costs what decline says: ally_relations (the opinion of the nation you let down), prestige, and end_treaty (the treaty lapses). The AI always honours a bound obligation unless it would have to fight an ally or a pact partner.

crisis._note: Mobilization as a diplomatic act (Diplomacy.step_day). Allies bound only defensively (defensive_only) are not called up. A nation whose mobilization reaches alarm_level alarms each land neighbour it is not allied with or at war with, once: alarm_relations is added to their opinion of it, they resent it (alarm_grievance), and their allies are called up. An AI nation answers whoever alarms it with match_response times their mobilization, or call_response times that of whoever alarmed its ally, and eases back by ai_step_down a day when nothing threatens it. A nation called to join a war mobilizes to called_level and joins when it reaches join_mobilization. Nations at war are pushed up to war_floor by war_step_up a day. A war with no casus belli needs min_mobilization first. The alarm clears once mobilization falls below alarm_clear_level.

peace._note: War score and peace (scripts/sim/peace.gd). Score is -100..100 from a nation's side of one pairwise war: ground held (occupation_points times the share of the other nation's population and GDP, weighted), the capital, and battles won (battle_per_kmen points per thousand men the loser lost, scaled by how lopsided, capped; they fade by decay_per_month). The side that takes terms pays for them in score: a province costs province_scale times its share (half if the taker already holds it, doubled for a capital); an indemnity costs indemnity_points_per_year times its share of revenue times its years; the clauses have flat prices. A nation that has lost its capital to the taker pays nothing. ai: a nation made to give refuses while its own score is above accept_loss; a white peace is refused while its score is above refuse_white_when_winning; a losing AI (seek_peace_score) offers the ground held, up to surrender_budget_share of the enemy's score; a long stalemate offers white peace; a refused proposer waits refuse_cooldown_days; making peace alone costs separate_peace_relations with those still fighting.

war_support._note: War support (scripts/sim/war_support.gd), 0..100. A government sets what a nation starts with and returns to in peace (recovery_per_month). At war it falls each month by weariness plus casualty_weight times the share of its men lost that month, blockade_weight times the blockade, and occupied_weight times the share of its people under enemy control; a battle won raises it by win_bonus (home_win_bonus on its own soil) and a battle lost lowers it by loss_penalty. While at war it multiplies tax and recruitment (economy_mult) and the fighting power of its armies (morale_mult) along a curve through the at_0, at_50 and at_100 values. At or below floor an AI accepts any terms it can be made to pay and seeks peace; at or below white_peace_below it is forced into a white peace with every enemy it is not clearly losing to (score at least white_peace_score); at surrender_at it can be made to give anything. A war with no casus belli also costs support (casus_belli.war_support).

plans._note: War plans (scenario.json, war_plans): an AI nation at war with `enemy` for delay_days declares war on `through` (a neutral in the way) with no casus belli, as soon as its mobilization allows it. It pays the usual price: world opinion, prestige, war support, and the neutral's guarantors are called. The player's nation never acts on a plan.

actions._note: Player diplomacy (Diplomacy.propose_treaty, Diplomacy.gift). A proposal is accepted when the other nation's opinion of the proposer is at least treaty_accept for the kind; an alliance also needs the two not to be in opposed blocs. A gift of N million raises the receiver's opinion by gift_relation_per_million times N, to at most gift_max_relation more per gift.

points._note: Diplomacy points (Nation.diplomacy_points): a nation's stock of diplomatic effort, spent by the commands DeclareWar, ProposeTreaty, CancelTreaty and Gift (costs below; an AI nation's own internal moves, such as joining a war it is bound to, are free) and earned each month: income.base, plus prestige_weight per point of prestige, plus top_output_bonus for the top_output_count nations by output, never below income.min. The stock cannot pass max. A refused treaty proposal gives refusal_refund of its cost back. purchase: pay base_cost GBP millions for a batch of points, the price rising by price_growth with each purchase and easing back by price_decay each month. improve: improve_relations starts a project that adds monthly to the opinion of the pair (and base_monthly to what it settles at) for months, at most max_active at once. prestige: a battle won earns battle_win, peace terms earn the taker peace_per_score a point of their cost (at most peace_cap, the loser loses peace_loser_share of that), a new alliance or guarantee earns the treaty value, and all of it fades by decay_per_month. Other income sources: the diplomatic service program and the foreign ministry building (see economy.json). A scenario nation can set its own start with diplomacy_points.
